patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches include a prominent rectangular input field in the main content area, implying a searchable page or site search control with submit behavior.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: At minimum the field needs input handling and submit behavior. Depending on implementation it may also support enter-to-submit and possibly suggestions, but the sketch only clearly implies search submission.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not show a search button, icon, autocomplete list, or whether results update live versus on submit.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The visible text input/search field implies a form submission path that requires handling empty or invalid submissions.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Validate that the field is usable before submit, preserve entered value, and provide feedback if submission is blocked or fails.
patterns_found.ambiguities: Because the field could be a simple search box, validation may be minimal and limited to empty-state handling.

sketch_notes: These sketches are extremely low fidelity and mostly depict static content blocks rather than explicit interactive widgets. The only consistently defensible JavaScript implication across mobile and desktop is a search/form input requiring submit handling and basic validation. No clear hamburger, dropdowns, tabs, accordions, modals, sticky behavior, load-more controls, or scroll-triggered UI are visibly indicated in the sketches themselves, even if such features may exist in the reference HTML.
